request.system:
You are a Magic: The Gathering set designer filling slots in a design skeleton.

You emit structured card data, never rules text. The rules text is rendered from
the structure you emit, so anything you cannot express in the given schema does
not exist in this set. Design inside the schema rather than around it.

Hard rules:
- Fill exactly the slots you are given, one card each, echoing each slotId verbatim.
- Respect every constraint on a slot: card kind, mana value window, colour, allowed effects.
- A card in a coloured slot must have at least one coloured mana pip of that colour and no other colour.
- Colourless slots take a mana cost of generic mana only.
- Never invent keywords, effects, costs, or card types. The schema is the whole vocabulary.
- Names must be evocative, unique across the set, and 40 characters or fewer.
- Power and toughness must be normal for the mana value; a two-mana 5/5 is a bug, not a design.
request.prompt:
<task>
<set_brief>
Set: Hearthglass Vigil (HRT), 20 cards.
Theme: A watch-fort of lamp-lit glass on a cold northern moor, held through a winter that will not end. Wardens stand the wall in shifts and the lamps are fed all night; what a warden leaves behind on the stones keeps working after the warden falls. Flavour is cold, patient and lamp-lit: frost on glass, oil and wick, banked coals, long watches, and the sound of something moving out past the last light.
Mechanics:
- Vigil: A warden keeps its post. The body carries its own rules text - a standing bonus or a promise that pays out when it enters, attacks or dies - instead of a spell doing the work for it. (abilities: static, triggered; colours: WG)
- Emberwork: Lamp-glass is spent, never hoarded. A permanent pays itself away, or taps its own heat, for a burst of fire. (effects: dealDamage; abilities: activated; colours: R)
- Deepwatch: The night shift reads the dark, thins what is coming and keeps its own hand full. (effects: millCards, drawCards; colours: UB)

Archetype intent:
- WG wants wardens that are worth the mana on the turn they land and still worth it three turns later.
- UB wants card flow and a mill clock as an alternate finish.
- WR wants cheap bodies that convert into damage before the wall gives.
</set_brief>

<slots>
CU01: common U creature, role creature, MV 2
  keywords: none - print a vanilla body with a strong name and creature types
CU02: common U creature, role creature, MV 3, keywords: flying
  keywords: exactly [flying], applied by the skeleton; design the body around them
CU03: common U instant, role protectiveInstant, MV 2, effects: returnToHand
  effects: exactly 1 entry, of kind returnToHand - a second entry could only repeat the first, which the DSL rejects
  note: DSL v0 has no protection or hexproof; the slot saves a creature by bouncing it.
</slots>

<effect_vocabulary>
- returnToHand: no parameters; target.kind: targetCreature
</effect_vocabulary>

<already_printed>
Names already used (do not repeat, do not echo): Frostlantern Owl, Wallwatch Sentinel, Verdict of the Last Lamp
</already_printed>

<task>Design 3 card(s), one per slot listed above, in slot order.</task>
</task>
